title: Co-applicant Home Loans: EMI, Tax Benefits & Credit Score Impact
description: Adding a co-applicant can significantly boost your home loan eligibility by combining incomes. Both co-applicants can individually claim tax deductions on pri.

faq.q: Can a non-owner be a co-applicant for a home loan?
faq.a: Yes, a non-owner can be a co-applicant, typically as a guarantor for the loan. However, to claim tax benefits on the home loan, the co-applicant usually needs to be a co-owner of the property as well.

faq.q: Who can be a co-applicant for a home loan?
faq.a: Generally, close family members like your spouse, parents, siblings, or adult children can be co-applicants. The relationship criteria may vary slightly between lenders.

faq.q: What happens if one co-applicant defaults on the EMI?
faq.a: All co-applicants are jointly and severally liable for the entire loan. If one defaults, the lender can pursue the other co-applicants for the full outstanding amount, and both their credit scores will be negatively impacted.

faq.q: Can I remove a co-applicant from a home loan?
faq.a: Removing a co-applicant is a complex process. It usually requires the bank's approval, re-evaluation of the remaining applicant's eligibility, and potentially refinancing the loan. Legal changes to property ownership may also be necessary.

faq.q: Are there any disadvantages to having a co-applicant home loan?
faq.a: The primary disadvantage is shared liability. Both applicants are equally responsible for the loan, and any financial misstep by one can affect the other's credit score and financial standing.

faq.q: Do NRIs have special rules for co-applicant home loans?
faq.a: NRIs can apply for joint home loans, often with a resident Indian as a co-applicant. The tax benefits and eligibility criteria generally remain similar, but specific documentation and FEMA regulations for NRIs might apply, as detailed by the RBI ([https://rbi.org.in](https://rbi.org.in)).

faq.q: Is it mandatory to have a co-applicant for a home loan?
faq.a: No, it is not mandatory. You can apply for a home loan individually if your income and credit profile meet the lender's eligibility criteria for the desired loan amount.
